objective: TRIPLE-SHIELD-20261023-001 found that lone contradiction lines of three-place tiling worlds have unequal counts in the two twists that differ by the dual of their class, while two-literal lines with one coin per edge are shielded. A lone line is checked against three cylinders only, and the two twists check different other classes. First decide whether the inequality belongs to the line itself (pure lines, all of whose contradictions run along the line's class, still differ) or to what the event fails to exclude (pure lines are shielded); then find the local structure behind whichever holds and test it as a counting law.
status: Complete 2026-10-23. Answer: the largest three-place dual-pair ratios were mostly a blind spot, not the line seeing the twist. Proved: in every two-literal tiling world on a triangular torus, shared coins included, a configuration contradicts along no class, one class, or every odd class (the doubly allowed tiling makes the parity of every closed implication walk the relative twist of its class), so lone lines are line events there and shared-coin failures are genuine. Three-place worlds break this trichotomy (certified; 12 of 30 placements selective on every torus computed), so their lone lines can contradict along unchecked classes: nearly all lone lines of the most lopsided pairs do. Measured (frozen experiment, partially supported, independently checked): lines pure among eight classes still differ across dual pairs (395160 against 547584 for placement 111 on 3 x 4); the prediction that the 54 and 62 families have no pure lone lines on 3 x 4 failed (6 and 1176 in one twist). Qualifies TRIPLE-SHIELD-20261023-001-D001. Recommendation: Continue with a fresh epic on directional rigidity (which contacts are all or nothing in direction); interest 2/3; deferred to the owner.
title: What a three-place line sees
